title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is useful for teams considering switching from Jira to Plane, possibly due to the core use case of issue tracking and project management, and the key reason being the desire for more control over their data and costs. Teams who value data ownership and customization may benefit from this comparison.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira has a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows teams to have full control over their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Jira has a more complex setup process, while Plane is relatively simpler to set up.
* Scalability: Jira is more scalable, with built-in support for large teams, while Plane may require more manual configuration for large teams.
* Integration: Jira has built-in integration with other Atlassian tools, while Plane has integration with GitHub and other development tools.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Jira
* Pros:
  + Scalable and reliable
  + Integrates well with other Atlassian tools
  + Robust feature set
  + Good customer support
  + Widely adopted and recognized
* Cons:
  + Expensive, especially for large teams
  + Complex setup process
  + Limited customization options
  + Data stored on Jira's servers
  + Can be overwhelming for small teams
### Plane
* Pros:
  + Free and self-hosted
  + Highly customizable
  + Integrates well with GitHub and other development tools
  + Gives teams full control over their data
  + Simple setup process
* Cons:
  + Limited scalability without manual configuration
  + Limited support for non-technical teams
  + May require additional development resources for customization
  + Limited integration with non-development tools
  + Still a relatively new tool with some rough edges

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams that need a robust and scalable project management tool, and are willing to pay for it. Jira's integration with other Atlassian tools and its wide adoption make it a good choice for teams that are already invested in the Atlassian ecosystem. On the other hand, Plane is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that value data ownership and customization, and are looking for a free and self-hosted solution. Plane's simplicity and flexibility make it a good choice for teams that are looking for a lightweight project management tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format using Jira's built-in export tool.
2. Set up a Plane instance and configure it to match your Jira setup.
3. Use Plane's import tool to import your Jira data into Plane.
4. Configure any additional features or integrations in Plane as needed.
5. Test your Plane setup to ensure that everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Plane is still a relatively new tool, and while it shows a lot of promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Plane's scalability requires manual configuration, which can be a challenge for large teams. However, for small to medium-sized teams that value data ownership and customization, Plane is definitely worth considering, and we recommend switching to Plane if you are a small team looking for a free and self-hosted solution.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that do not need advanced project management features
* Teams that value data ownership and customization
* Development teams that already use GitHub and other development tools
* Teams that are looking for a free and self-hosted solution
* Teams that do not need integration with non-development tools

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, which means that you can use it without paying any monthly fees.
### Is Plane as scalable as Jira?
No, Plane's scalability requires manual configuration, which can be a challenge for large teams.
### Can I integrate Plane with other tools?
Yes, Plane integrates well with GitHub and other development tools, but may require additional development resources for customization.
### Is Plane suitable for non-technical teams?
No, Plane may require additional technical resources for setup and customization, which can be a challenge for non-technical teams.
### Can I export my Jira data to Plane?
Yes, you can export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using Plane's import tool.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Dropbox and Nextcloud are cloud storage solutions that enable individuals and teams to store, share, and collaborate on files. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and organizations considering a switch from a proprietary cloud storage service to a self-hosted alternative. The core use case for both tools is file storage and sharing, and someone would switch to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Dropbox charges a monthly fee per user, while Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Nextcloud allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Dropbox's terms of service grant the company certain rights to user data.
* Setup complexity: Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for self-hosting, compared to Dropbox's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Nextcloud can be more scalable than Dropbox, especially for large organizations, since it can be self-hosted on the user's own servers.
* Integration with OnlyOffice: Nextcloud has native integration with OnlyOffice for document editing, while Dropbox relies on third-party integrations for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $499.50-$829/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,998-$3,316/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Dropbox:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of third-party integrations
* Robust security features
* Cross-platform compatibility
* Limited control over data ownership
**Nextcloud:**
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* High scalability and customization
* Native integration with OnlyOffice
* Free to use with self-hosting
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Dropbox is suitable for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and don't require full control over their data. It's ideal for teams that need a straightforward, user-friendly cloud storage solution with a wide range of third-party integrations. On the other hand, Nextcloud is perfect for large organizations or teams that require high scalability, customization, and full control over their data. It's also suitable for individuals and teams that value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Dropbox in ZIP format.
2. Set up your Nextcloud instance on your own server or use a pre-configured appliance.
3. Use the Nextcloud WebDAV interface to import your exported data.
4. Configure any necessary settings, such as user accounts and permissions.
5. Test your Nextcloud instance to ensure a smooth transition.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready solution for most users, offering a wide range of features and a high degree of customization. However, one technical limitation worth noting is the requirement for technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted instance. For most users, we recommend switching to Nextcloud if they value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own self-hosted solution.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of 5-10 users that don't require a wide range of third-party integrations
* Large organizations with over 100 users that need high scalability and customization
* Individuals who value data ownership and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own self-hosted solution
* Teams that require native integration with OnlyOffice for document editing
* Users who don't need cross-platform compatibility

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud for free?
Yes, Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting. You will need to cover the cost of your own server and maintenance.
### Is Nextcloud more secure than Dropbox?
Nextcloud offers a high degree of security, including encryption and access controls, but the level of security ultimately depends on the user's setup and configuration.
### Can I integrate Nextcloud with other tools and services?
Yes, Nextcloud has a wide range of integrations with third-party tools and services, including OnlyOffice and Collabora Online.
### Is Nextcloud suitable for small teams?
Yes, Nextcloud can be suitable for small teams, but it may require more technical expertise to set up and maintain compared to Dropbox.
### Can I migrate my data from Dropbox to Nextcloud?
Yes, you can export your data from Dropbox and import it into Nextcloud using the WebDAV interface.
meta_description: Nextcloud, a free self-hosted cloud storage solution, offers full data control and scalability. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Zoom data, follow the Jitsi Meet import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

## Overview
Monday.com and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. The key reason someone would switch is to have full ownership of their data and a more customizable platform.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Monday.com charges $9-$19 per user per month, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows full data ownership, while Monday.com stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Monday.com has a more straightforward setup process, while Plane requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Plane is highly scalable due to its self-hosted nature, while Monday.com has limitations on its scalability.
* Integration difference: Plane has a more open API for custom integrations, while Monday.com has a more limited set of pre-built integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Monday.com | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9-$19/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $450-$950/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,800-$3,800/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Monday.com:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of pre-built integrations
* Good customer support
* Limited customization options
* Data stored on proprietary servers
**Plane:**
* Full data ownership and control
* Highly customizable and scalable
* Free and self-hosted
* Steeper learning curve
* Limited pre-built integrations

## When to Choose Each
Monday.com is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who need a straightforward project management tool with a wide range of pre-built integrations. It is ideal for teams who do not require full data ownership and are willing to pay a monthly fee per user. Plane, on the other hand, is suitable for larger teams or organizations that require full control over their data and a high degree of customization. It is ideal for teams with technical expertise who can self-host and maintain their own servers.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from Monday.com in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Plane server and configure the database.
3. Use the Plane import tool to migrate data from the exported file.
4. Configure any custom integrations or workflows in Plane.
5. Test the migrated data and workflows to ensure everything is working as expected.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users due to its steep learning curve and limited pre-built integrations. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane requires a high degree of technical expertise for self-hosting and maintenance. However, for teams who require full data ownership and control, Plane is a good option, and we recommend switching from Monday.com to Plane for teams with technical expertise and a need for customization.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with technical expertise who need full data ownership and control
* Medium-sized teams who require a high degree of customization and scalability
* Large organizations with existing self-hosting infrastructure
* Teams who do not require pre-built integrations with third-party tools
* Developers who need a highly customizable platform for project management

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, but you will need to pay for server costs.

Plane allows for full data ownership and control, which can be more secure than storing data on proprietary servers.
